sources.title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing
Diagnosing sample ratio mismatch in online controlled experiments

concepts.definition: A randomized controlled experiment comparing a control and a changed version on a predefined metric.
A metric that must not get worse during a test, such as refund rate or page speed.
A difference between the planned and observed traffic split, which signals a broken test.
Checking results repeatedly and stopping when they look significant, which inflates false positives.

questions.q: About how many visitors per group are needed to detect a change from 3.0% to 3.3% conversion?
questions.a: About 52,000 per group using n = 16 p(1 - p) / delta squared.

questions.q: Why randomize by user rather than by page view?
questions.a: So that a person sees the same version on every visit, avoiding contamination between versions.

questions.q: What is a novelty effect, and how do you handle it?
questions.a: Users react to a change because it is new; run the test long enough for the effect to settle.
